intro.1: {{Sawasdee krub|hello}}! There you are. I'm Somchai, but everyone here calls me Lung — "uncle".
intro.2: Thirty years fixing phones on this beach. Now my hands shake a little… and the hammock is calling. The stall is yours.
intro.3: You don't have much: a mat, a cheap screwdriver, a suction cup. With the right head, it's enough. {{Mai pen rai|no worries}}!
intro.4: Before you touch a customer's phone, let's strip this old Fone 8 together. It's a wreck: nobody cries if you slip.
intro.5: Click the work mat to sit at the bench. I'll guide you step by step.

lesson.power_off: Rule number one: ALWAYS power off before opening. A live phone is a phone that can fry.
lesson.unscrew: See the two tiny screws by the charge port? They're pentalobes, five points: you need the P2 bit. Select the driver and hold on the screw.
lesson.place_screw: Every screw has a home. Put it on the magnetic mat, one cell per group: soon you'll see why it's life or death.
lesson.heat: The display is glued. Cold, it cracks: heat the edges until the adhesive softens. Watch the bar: too little won't give, too much cooks the screen.
lesson.suction: Now the suction cup: press on the glass and pull up gently. Hear the pop? A gap opened.
lesson.cut: Slip the pick in and drag it all around the edge: the orange strip turns green where you've cut. Where it's red, stay close to the edge: flex cables run under there. Cut one and the display is scrap.
lesson.open: Now take the Hand (key 1) and click the display: it opens like a book, from the right side. Never yank: it's still attached by its cables.
lesson.disconnect_battery: Stop! Before touching any connector, unplug the BATTERY. Remove the bracket and use the plastic spudger — never metal. No power, no sparks.
lesson.disconnect: Good. Now the other connectors: a gentle pry and they click. Delicate as butterfly wings.
lesson.remove: Once a part is free of screws, brackets and connectors, lift it with the tweezers and lay it on the mat. It stays where you leave it.
lesson.pull_tab: The battery is held by stretchy adhesive tabs. Pull slowly, low and steady. Yank and they snap — then you need alcohol and a lot of patience.
lesson.pry_pad: This part is only lightly glued: pry gently with the spudger.
lesson.teardown_done: Look at that: a whole phone, piece by piece. Every part you remove goes into your encyclopedia. Now the hard part: putting it back!
lesson.install: Reassembly goes in reverse: bottom parts first. Click a part on the mat to put it back.
lesson.pick_screw: Now you get the mat. Screws are NOT all the same: a long screw in a short hole pierces the board beneath. It's called long screw damage, and it has killed more phones than seawater.
lesson.screw_in: Hold to tighten, release when the needle is in the green. Too little: it rattles. Too much: you strip it, and I glare at you from the hammock.
lesson.connect: Press connectors until they click. All of them, except one that waits…
lesson.connect_battery: …the battery. Always last, so nothing is live while you work. First out, last in.
lesson.close: Close the display and put the two pentalobes back. Then power on.
lesson.done: Now the final test: check every function before handing a phone back. Press 'Final test'.

after_test.1: Everything works! You've got good hands, {{nong|kid}}. Better than mine at twenty… almost.
after_test.2: Look, here comes Noi from the bar next door. Her phone doesn't last till evening. Listen to the customer, diagnose, quote an honest price.
after_test.3: Here, a new battery: my gift for your first job. Order the next ones from Mr. Chai, who comes by boat every morning.

first_customer.counter: Click the customer to hear what she needs.
first_customer.accepted: Order taken! The phone is on the bench: click the mat to start. Just a battery swap: follow the guide.
first_customer.delivered: Your first review! Stars bring customers, customers bring baht.

first_purchase.1: With your first earnings, buy a better tool. Open the tablet (Tab) and check the catalog.
first_purchase.done: Great pick. Every tool changes your work: fewer mistakes, more speed, new repairs.
first_purchase.bye: I'm off to the hammock. If you run out of money, you know where to find me… {{Chok dee|good luck}}!
